chunks: What Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Hakam ibn Hukaym, who said:

I asked Aba 'Abd Allah عليه السلام about a man who forgets a rak'ah from his salat (prayer), or a sajdah, or more than that, then remembers. He said: He makes up exactly that itself. I said: Does he repeat the salat (prayer)? He said: No.

key_terms.بِعَيْنِهِ: exactly that very missed act itself
key_terms.رَكْعَةً: a unit of salat (prayer) that was omitted
key_terms.سَجْدَةً: a prostration that was omitted from the salat (prayer)
key_terms.صَلَاتِهِ: his salat (prayer), the ritual prayer under discussion
key_terms.يَقْضِي: he makes up or performs later what was missed

ai.seo_question: If someone forgets a rak'ah or sajdah in salat (prayer), must he repeat the whole prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding one who forgets part of his salat (prayer), such as a rak'ah or sajdah, and later remembers it. The Imam عليه السلام states that he should make up the missed part itself and does not need to repeat the entire salat (prayer).
